subject.title: [Bug]: Potential resource leak in runBoundTurnWithMissingThreadRecovery -- retry not wrapped in try/finally after thread spawn

question: Should Codex app-server bound conversations keep a persistent thread subscription across turns, or should OpenClaw reattach and unsubscribe around each bound turn including missing-thread recovery retries?
rationale: The source-level leak concern is real enough to keep open, but the previous broad cleanup attempt showed that changing subscription ownership can break later bound-turn delivery without an explicit lifecycle decision.

options.title: Preserve persistent subscriptions
options.body: Treat the replacement thread subscription as intentional session state unless the binding is cleared, and add tests/documentation that make this lifecycle explicit before closing or narrowing the issue.

options.title: Use per-turn reattach and cleanup
options.body: Change bound turns to reattach before each `turn/start` and unsubscribe after completion or rejection, with regression tests for two consecutive bound turns and retry failure.

options.title: Narrow cleanup to failed recovery only
options.body: Only clean up the replacement thread when maintainers decide a failed retry should not leave a reusable binding, and cover that behavior with focused tests.

recommendation.title: Preserve persistent subscriptions
recommendation.body: Treat the replacement thread subscription as intentional session state unless the binding is cleared, and add tests/documentation that make this lifecycle explicit before closing or narrowing the issue.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses the original recovery behavior and the current app-server cleanup helper ownership, both of which appear in `steipete`-committed history.
